nodes.text: Come in quietly, if you would — the tinctures settle better in a calm room. I'm Wyn. Wounds, weariness, and everything the mountain does to lowland lungs: somewhere on these shelves is the answer.

choices.text: You trade with the Last Lamp?

nodes.text: More than the lowlands credit. Ledge-flowers that bloom late and hold long. Sagewort gone small and fierce with the altitude — half the dose does twice the work, mind that if you buy it. And snow-moss the rams won't touch, which is how you know it's medicine. If it tastes pleasant up here, it's a vegetable.

A crate of tinctures down to Edda's lamp every season, since before the trade had my name on it. She sends back the empties and a note that says the same thing every year: 'still alive, no thanks needed, the amber one wants more bite.' From Edda, that's a warm embrace. Her sister keeps our shrine — the stubbornness runs in the family; only the altitude differs.
Green for wounds, amber for weariness, and the salve for everything the road rubs raw. Gathered high, brewed slow.
